record.paper_title: Discrepancy estimates for sequences: new results and open problems
record.original_question: Given positive integers d1,...,dl with d1+...+dl=d and pairwise coprime bases q1,...,ql, determine functions g(N) as small as possible and f(N) as large as possible such that, for almost all d-dimensional Halton-Niederreiter sequences whose i-th component is a d_i-dimensional digital sequence in base q_i, the discrepancy D_N satisfies D_N = Omega(f(N)) and D_N = O(g(N)).

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5 For given d1, . . . , dl ∈ N with d1+. . .+dl = d and given coprime bases q1, . . . , ql determine g(N) as small as possible and f(N) as large as possible such that we have: for the discrepancy DN of almost all Halton-Niederreiter sequences with di-dimensional components in base qi; i = 1, . . . , l we have DN = Ω(f(N)) and DN = O(g(N)).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d, l \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $d_1,\dots,d_l \in \mathbb{N}$ with $d_1+\cdots+d_l = d$. Let $q_1,\dots,q_l$ be pairwise coprime integer bases ($q_i \ge 2$). For each $i$, let $\mathbf{x}^{(i)} = (\mathbf{x}^{(i)}_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be a $d_i$-dimensional digital sequence in base $q_i$ (a digital $(t_i,d_i)$-sequence in the sense of Niederreiter, parameterized by infinite generating matrices over $\mathbb{F}_{q_i}$). The associated Halton–Niederreiter sequence in $[0,1)^d$ is
$$\mathbf{x}_n = (\mathbf{x}^{(1)}_n, \mathbf{x}^{(2)}_n, \dots, \mathbf{x}^{(l)}_n), \qquad n = 0, 1, 2, \dots .$$
For any sequence $(\mathbf{x}_n)_{n\ge 0}$ in $[0,1)^d$ define the star discrepancy of its first $N$ terms by
$$D_N = \sup_{\mathbf{a}\in[0,1]^d}\left| \frac{1}{N} \#\{0\le n < N : \mathbf{x}_n \in [\mathbf{0},\mathbf{a})\} - \prod_{j=1}^d a_j \right|.$$
Equip the space of generating-matrix data parametrizing all such Halton–Niederreiter sequences with the natural product Haar/Lebesgue measure.

Determine functions $f(N)$ as large as possible and $g(N)$ as small as possible such that, for almost every choice of generating data,
$$D_N = \Omega(f(N)) \quad \text{and} \quad D_N = O(g(N)) \quad (N\to\infty).$$
artifact.status_search_result: Metrical discrepancy results have been established for related Halton–Kronecker hybrid sequences (analogous to Khintchine and W. M. Schmidt theorems), but no source found in the search provides matching upper and lower metrical bounds for general Halton–Niederreiter hybrids with arbitrary coprime bases and digital components. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Metrical results on the discrepancy of Halton–Kronecker sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Metrical results for the discrepancy of Halton–Kronecker sequences which are similar to results for the pure Kronecker sequences obtained by Khintchine and by W.M. Schmidt.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous metrical results exist for Halton–Kronecker hybrids but not for the digital Halton–Niederreiter setting in question.

status_evidence.title: On hybrid sequences built from Niederreiter-Halton sequences and Kronecker sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Distribution properties of subsequences of Niederreiter-Halton sequences generated by joining digital (T,s)-sequences in different prime bases.
status_evidence.claim: Deterministic, not metrical (almost-all), discrepancy bounds are studied for these hybrids.
